customManagers.description: The Rust toolchain pinned in every workflow (`toolchain: <X.Y.Z>`, matching devbox.json's rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt). The literal version is deliberately NOT written here — see the cargo-nextest manager below, where a version quoted in prose is exactly what rotted (issue #648). dtolnay/rust-toolchain publishes toolchain versions as BRANCHES with only a `v1` tag, so pinning the ref instead (`@1.97.1`) would be a version Renovate could never bump; the action stays at `@v1` and the toolchain rides an input, which splits the two concerns — the github-actions rule bumps the action, this manager bumps the toolchain. Without it the pin would silently rot, which is the failure mode that made floating `@stable` attractive in the first place. CORRECTION (2026-08-21): this description used to open 'The github-actions manager cannot see this: it reads the `uses:` ref.' That is FALSE now and the falsehood had teeth. Renovate's github-actions manager carries a registry of community actions whose version lives in an INPUT rather than the ref (`lib/modules/manager/github-actions/community.ts`), and `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is in it: it reads the same `toolchain:` string this manager matches and emits it as depName `rust`, depType `uses-with`, datasource `rust-version`. So the toolchain now arrives down TWO lanes, and until the `uses-with` packageRule below was added the second one landed in the automerging `GitHub Actions` group — PR #623 (`renovate/github-actions`, automerge enabled, no `manual-review` label) and PR #624 (this manager's lane, held) proposed byte-identical 1.97.1 -> 1.98.0 diffs on the same day. Only an unrelated red CI kept #623 from merging itself. The duplicate PR is now deliberate and is NOT suppressed: both lanes are held for a human, and two independent detectors on a pin whose named failure mode is SILENT ROT are worth one redundant PR per Rust release. They self-resolve — the lanes edit the same lines, so merging either makes the other conflict and `rebaseWhen: conflicted` autocloses it.

The cargo-nextest version pinned in every workflow (`tool: cargo-nextest@<X.Y.Z>`, matching devbox.json). The literal version is deliberately NOT written here, matching the convention ci.yml's own header states: a version quoted in prose rots on the next bump with nothing to catch it, and this description had been claiming 0.9.140 for the eleven days devbox.json spent on 0.9.143 (issue #648). Read the value off devbox.json. Same reasoning as the toolchain manager above: taiki-e/install-action is pinned at `@v2` and the tool version rides an input. `taiki-e/install-action` is NOT in Renovate's community-actions registry today (checked 2026-08-21), so this manager is currently the only lane that sees the pin — but that is exactly what was true of `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` until it was added, so the claim is written as an expiry date rather than a property. The `uses-with` rule below holds this pin the day the registry grows an entry for it, WITHOUT anyone having to notice.

packageRules.description: Patch bumps are in-range for Cargo and gated on CI (build + build-macos + build-windows + fast test tier).

Minor bumps automerge on green CI — but only for crates already at 1.0 or later, where a minor is genuinely backwards-compatible under semver. This is the `matchCurrentVersion` the earlier note here recommended, applied 2026-07-30 after an automerge-eligible portable-pty 0.8 -> 0.9 landed PSUEDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR and stalled every Windows pane. 0.x minors are handled by the next rule.

A 0.x minor is a BREAKING change as far as Cargo is concerned (0.8 -> 0.9 is not compatible), so it is a major in everything but Renovate's label. Held for a human, matching the intent 'automerge anything that is not a major'. Stated as its own rule rather than left to the default so the intent is explicit and labelled: portable-pty 0.9.0 reached main through exactly this gap.

Renovate ignores this crate entirely: no PRs, and no Dependency Dashboard entry to remember to check. portable-pty is held at =0.8.1 deliberately (see the Cargo.toml comment): 0.9.0 sets PSUEDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR, so ConPTY withholds a Windows pane's output until a terminal answers ESC[6n, stalling every pane. Renovate re-proposed 0.9.0 within minutes of the v0.35.1 release; a standing PR for a pin held on purpose is pure noise, and the unpin is gated on a PRODUCT decision (native Windows support), not on a version becoming available — so no dependency bot can know when the time is right. Safe to silence because the `security` CI job runs `cargo audit` on every PR and every push to main, so a vulnerability in this crate surfaces there regardless of Renovate. The reminder to revisit lives in the Cargo.toml comment and the tracking issue, i.e. where the Windows decision will actually be made.

Ordinary devbox packages automerge on green CI. Note what green means for one of these PRs: ci.yml's `changes` gate skips all four required jobs when a Renovate PR touches nothing but devbox.json/devbox.lock, and GitHub counts a skipped required check as passing, so the only check that has actually LOOKED at the change is the `devbox` job. That is acceptable for vals/gh/jq/ffmpeg, which nothing else in the repository pins. It is not acceptable for the five toolchain packages, which the next rule takes out of this group.

Devbox toolchain packages, held for the SAME human who holds the workflow pins below. These five are the devbox half of a version pinned TWICE: `.github/workflows/` carries the other half (`toolchain:` for the four Rust components, `tool: cargo-nextest@` for nextest), and the two halves have to move as one change, because `cargo test-fast` in a devbox shell and `cargo nextest run` in CI are the same claim only while they agree. Issue #648: until this rule existed the two halves had OPPOSITE automerge policies — this group merged itself unattended while the `custom.regex` rule below held the workflow half for a human — so they separated on every release BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by anyone forgetting. cargo-nextest reached 0.9.143 in devbox.json via automerged #510 on 2026-08-11 and ci.yml sat on 0.9.140 for eleven days, invisible until somebody diffed the two files. Removing the asymmetry is the fix. GROUPING THE TWO LANES WAS THE OTHER OPTION AND IS WORSE: a shared `groupName` bundles the two PRs when both lanes have an update, but it cannot make the lanes OFFER the same version, and they routinely do not — the devbox datasource is nixpkgs, which never carried nextest 0.9.141 or 0.9.142 (both published to crates.io the same afternoon as 0.9.143) and has no Rust 1.98.0 at all, which is why #647 is held open. So the common case is one lane holding an upgrade the other cannot match, and the grouped PR then contains exactly one half — the same drift, now wearing a title that says lockstep — while a group spanning `automerge: true` and `automerge: false` would have to be resolved by dropping automerge here anyway. WHAT THIS COSTS: two PRs per toolchain release that somebody must click, where the devbox one used to be free. The frequency is low (nextest roughly monthly, Rust roughly six-weekly, nixpkgs lagging both), and the click is not `read a diff` but `put the other half in this branch and merge once`, which is the work the lockstep requires however it is scheduled. It also does NOT gate anything by itself: a devbox-only PR skips all four required checks (see the rule above), so this is a label plus a human. `scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh` is the part with teeth — the `devbox` job, the only ungated one, runs it, and `cargo test-fast` runs it via xtask/linkage-check. Naming five packages is an enumeration, which #641 argued against for the depType whitelist; it is a different thing here — not a blacklist of names caught misbehaving, but the closed set of devbox packages duplicated into `.github/workflows/`. If that set grows and this list does not follow, the guard still catches the drift, so the enforcement does not depend on this rule being complete.

Lock file maintenance is disabled for devbox.lock, because Renovate resolves the lock inside its own throwaway container and devbox writes an ABSOLUTE path for `path:` flake entries. PR #348 therefore added a `path:gcloud#google-cloud-sdk` entry whose `resolved` field pointed at `path:/tmp/renovate/repos/github/vfarcic/dot-agent-deck/gcloud`, a directory that exists on no real machine; 77b5e87 removed it. The entry is not something devbox recreates — `devbox install` leaves the lock at 17 entries and resolves the local flake from devbox.json — so it is purely an artifact of where the bot ran, and every lock file maintenance run would re-add it. Actual devbox package bumps are unaffected: they still flow through the `Devbox packages` rule above, so only the wholesale lock refresh stops. Consequence to accept: the nixpkgs revisions pinned in devbox.lock now only move when a package bump moves them, so refresh them by hand (`devbox update`) if they drift too far.

Automerge covers ACTION REFS ONLY — `uses: owner/repo@ref`, which is depType `action`. This is a WHITELIST on purpose, and `matchDepTypes` is the load-bearing line in it. The github-actions manager emits six depTypes (`action`, `docker`, `container`, `service`, `github-runner`, `uses-with`), and this rule used to match the manager with no depType filter at all, so it automerged every one of them — including tool versions read out of an action's INPUTS. That is how the Rust toolchain pin acquired an automerging lane (see the customManager description above and the `uses-with` rule below). Whitelisting rather than excluding the one dep name observed misbehaving is the point: Renovate's input-detection registry is a list that GROWS, so a blacklist is only ever correct until the next release, whereas anything this manager learns to detect tomorrow falls OUTSIDE this rule and is held by default. The cost of being wrong in this direction is a PR someone has to click; in the other direction it is an unreviewed toolchain change on main.

Everything the github-actions manager extracts that is NOT an action ref is held for a human and labelled. Stated as its own rule rather than left to Renovate's automerge default, matching the convention of the 0.x-minor rule above: a hold that exists only as an absence is invisible on the PR page and impossible to grep for. `uses-with` is the one that matters here — it is a version string embedded in an action's inputs, which for this repo means the Rust toolchain (`dtolnay/rust-toolchain`'s `toolchain:`) and the docs site's Node (`actions/setup-node`'s `node-version:`), i.e. two TOOLCHAINS wearing a GitHub Actions costume. A toolchain bump is not an action bump: it changes what compiles, it is where new deny-by-default rustc lints and clippy lints arrive, and in this repo it must move in lockstep with devbox.json by hand. Worse, before this rule the toolchain rode the `GitHub Actions` GROUP, so a Rust bump could arrive bundled inside a PR titled 'update GitHub Actions' alongside a handful of ordinary `@v7` bumps and automerge without ever being read on its own. The remaining depTypes (container/service/docker images, `runs-on:` runner versions) are listed for completeness — this repo has none today, and if it grows one, a base image or runner change is also not something to land unread.

The workflow toolchain pins are held for a human even on a patch. They must stay in lockstep with devbox.json's rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt and cargo-nextest pins — that lockstep is the whole point of pinning them — so each PR needs the matching devbox bump alongside it. A Rust patch release is also exactly where a new clippy lint appears, which is a `-D warnings` failure to read rather than automerge. Corrected 2026-08-22 (issue #648): this description used to add `and nothing enforces it automatically`, and that sentence turned out to be a prediction rather than a caveat — the devbox half was automerging while this half waited, and cargo-nextest drifted 0.9.143/0.9.140 for eleven days. Two things changed. The devbox half is now held by the `Devbox toolchain packages` rule above, so both halves wait for the same person and land together. And the lockstep IS enforced automatically now: `scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh` compares the two files and fails, from `cargo test-fast` (so the three required build jobs and a contributor's local gate) and from ci.yml's `devbox` job (the one job no `changes` gate can skip). Landing this lane alone therefore turns the PR red rather than main. This rule is ALSO not the only hold on these pins and must not be read as one: the same `toolchain:` string is seen by the github-actions manager under a different dep name, and the depType rules above are what close that lane and any future one. Keep all of it — this one says WHY the pin is held, those say WHERE ELSE it can be reached from, and the guard is what notices when a hold is bypassed anyway.

Do not propose an npm package until it is three days old. pnpm 11 (arrived via #776) enforces a supply-chain policy that REJECTS lockfile entries for packages published within the last 24 hours — its own default, not configured here — so a PR opened hours after publication fails `desktop-web` at `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION, and one that MERGES leaves `main` red until the package ages out (issue #813). Measured twice in two days: lucide-react 1.38.0 merged via #790 and held `main` red ~16h, and 1.39.0 arrived on #809 at 1h28m old. The failure is time-based and self-healing, which is what makes it corrosive rather than merely annoying — a recurring red check that means nothing trains everyone to ignore red checks, and an unrelated PR opened in that window inherits it (#805 failed at 23h31m, 29 minutes short). Renovate's internalChecksFilter holds the update rather than opening a PR, so nothing is created for CI to reject. THREE days rather than 24 hours on purpose: pnpm evaluates the cutoff at install time, so matching the figure exactly leaves no margin for a PR opened at the boundary, and for the packages this actually affects — an icon set, test tooling, a docs site — three days costs nothing. SCOPED TO npm DELIBERATELY: pnpm's policy governs npm packages only, so cargo, devbox and github-actions lanes keep their current cadence; a global delay would change three lanes to fix a problem in one. NOTE the 24-hour figure is pnpm's default, not a value pinned in this repository — if it changes, or is later configured explicitly, this number has to track it, which is a two-halves-of-one-number problem of the same shape as #648 in a lane scripts/check-pin-lockstep.sh does not cover.

Deliberate EXACT pins in Cargo.toml, never automerged. crossterm's pin is load-bearing: `ui::ctrl_c0_byte` documents crossterm 0.28.1's decoder behaviour and `keyevent_ctrl_c0_matches_crossterm_decoder` guards it (PRD #227). See also #242 (crossterm 0.28.1 + 0.29.0 coexist because ratatui 0.30 pulls 0.29 via ratatui-crossterm). portable-pty is pinned at =0.8.1 because 0.9.0 sets PSUEDOCONSOLE_INHERIT_CURSOR, which makes ConPTY withhold a Windows pane's output until a terminal answers ESC[6n — see the Cargo.toml comment. WITHOUT this entry a 0.8 -> 0.9 bump counts as a `minor` for the cargo rule above and would AUTOMERGE, silently reintroducing the stall; that is how 0.9.0 landed the first time.
